title: Entropy-Budgeted Shared Memory for Multi-Agent Workflows
research_question: Can an entropy-budgeted shared-memory mechanism that compresses and selectively refreshes intermediate agent outputs improve end-to-end task success and token efficiency in multi-agent workflows compared with standard full-context message passing?
hypothesis: In multi-agent workflows, many intermediate messages are redundant or low-value; enforcing an uncertainty-aware memory budget that preserves only high-information artifacts and triggers refresh when uncertainty rises will improve coordination quality while reducing token cost and context saturation.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around routing, replanning, escalation, and decomposition in agentic workflows, suggesting this space is crowded. A clearer gap is memory and communication efficiency: current rejected proposals focus on which agent or model to use, not how shared intermediate state should be filtered under limited context. The self-adaptive systems material also highlights model uncertainty and heterogeneous goals as open future-work themes, which can be transferred into agent workflows by treating shared memory updates as adaptive decisions under uncertainty. This yields a distinct direction: optimize collaboration through information selection rather than yet another scheduler or verifier.
